items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: They even had their own conductor, an Italian conductor. And most of the guys in the band were Italian guys.

ctx.x: Yeah. I mean my grandfather initially was a professional trumpet player, my dad’s dad. He played the Panamanian Exposition of, what was that, 1908 or something like that. And he met my grandmother and she said, “Look if you want to marry me you’re going to have to get a job. A real job. Typical. And so he was in the New York City Sanitation Department a garbage man. But then after a while, but that was back in the days when the City had, every department had their own band. The Fire Department had their own band,…

Is there some, was there a big break for you when you look back on post-college then, was there a relationship with a particular musician or something that happened that you felt really opened things up?
